A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, central methods and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable. Reformatting and relocation do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4.1-4.4 and Appendix D report original LHIER, HyperMAtt and HCNN+ experiments, including retrieval, classification, runtime, VAE reconstruction/generation and component-ablation results.

after.justification: v4 retains original vision and EEG experiments and adds original node-classification experiments and graph-model ablations in Appendix E.4.

M1.justification: The curvature-aware update and tangent-space remapping procedure, centroid-based Riemannian AdamW, flexible tanh rescaling and rotation/boost convolution construction are retained. v4 expands their explanation and pseudocode; the graph study applies existing components without introducing an architecture change.

E1.justification: Appendix E.4 and Table 9 add node classification on Disease, Airport, PubMed and Cora, extending evaluation to graph data and a task absent from v3. The previously tabulated vision and EEG coverage remains, including ResNet-18 experiments moved into the appendix.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes MIC, XBM, HTL, MS, SoftTriple and PA without relocating them; NSoftmax, ProxyNCA++, Hyp and HIER remain. New Table 9 introduces the HyboNet reference comparison and evaluates alternatives using trivialized parameters and scaling-based manifold mapping. This substantially changes the reported comparison set.

E3.justification: Table 1 restricts metric-learning comparisons to ResNet-50 with 512-dimensional embeddings, dropping the previously reported 128-dimensional and Inception-BN configurations. The new graph protocol holds reference hyperparameters fixed across ablations and rescales inputs for the scaling-map variant. No changes to existing data splits or evaluation metrics are reported.

E4.justification: Table 9 adds graph ablations examining learnable curvature, AdamW, direct versus trivialized parameters, and tangent versus scaling-based mapping. The mapping comparison tests a central design choice not experimentally examined in v3. Existing image, metric-learning and EEG ablations remain in Tables 6-8, with expanded descriptions of their configurations.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 changes the reported HyperMAtt aggregation from three runs to ten while retaining mean and standard-deviation reporting. This establishes a reported run-count increase without explaining how the earlier run set was extended or replaced. Five-run reporting for ResNet-18 and VAEs remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 9 adds graph results: H3 leads on Airport, PubMed and Cora, but its Disease score of 94.82 trails reported HyboNet at 96 and H5 at 94.88. Table 2 revises HyperMAtt aggregates, including ERN from 78.01±1.30 to 77.98±1.60; Table 8 retains the old values. The ERN increase changes from 1.25% to 2.59%, which matches comparison with MAtt at 76.01; EEG-TCNet at 77.05 instead implies approximately 1.21%. Metric-learning baseline entries are removed, while matched ResNet, VAE and earlier ablation results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the hyperboloid constraint from an inner product of -1/K to -K and corrects the corresponding bound. Section 3.2 adds an explicit self-distance counterexample, and Appendix D adds an angle-preservation argument. The radial-distance preservation identity and Appendix C scaling derivation already appeared in v3, so the formal additions are limited.

C1.justification: The introduction expands its empirical contribution claim from three domains to five, adding graph embedding and explicitly including the already evaluated image-generation task. The abstract and contribution list remove the claim of state-of-the-art results in two domains. The central optimizer, scaling and computational-efficiency contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 adds substantive arguments that scaling mappings can violate numerical stability limits and misalign inputs with class prototypes, while interpreting preserved radii and angles as hierarchy and similarity information. Appendix F adds computational-cost and task-dependent mapping limitations. The graph discussion favors tangent mapping while acknowledging difficulty reproducing the Disease baseline.

D1.justification: v4 replaces the redacted code placeholder with a concrete repository address, identifies an RTX 4090 GPU and AMD EPYC 7543 CPU for ResNet-50 timings, and adds optimizer pseudocode, gradient-operation details and the fixed-curvature ablation value K=1. Conversely, it omits v3's explicit EEG fixed-curvature choice and independent encoder/decoder curvature-learning detail. These are documentation changes rather than demonstrated changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: v4 substantially clarifies the central contribution's relationship to prior work: Fu et al. and Guo et al. receive credit for tangent-based mapping, while Skopek et al. and Tabaghi et al. supply scaling-map alternatives. The contribution is positioned as extending mapping to optimization, gradients and momentum. It also removes the blanket statement about subsequent work not exploiting GeoOpt curvature learning and prunes NLP/VAE background citations.

P1.justification: Related work and Section 3.2 are extensively rewritten, and Section 4 is renamed and reorganized. HIER background and ResNet-18 discussion move into the appendices, while EEG and VAE descriptions are compressed. Proofs and Limitations appendices are added, the Impact Statement is replaced by Acknowledgements, and front matter and citation style change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with substantially reformatted tables and separate memory/time columns. Figure 1 moves into the appendix, and the ResNet-18 table moves from main-text Table 3 to Appendix Table 5. v4 adds color-highlighted Adam/AdamW pseudocode and graph Table 9 and shortens metric-learning Table 1. Both existing figures retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: v4 makes the central optimizer easier to assess by crediting prior mappings, explaining their tradeoffs, providing explicit pseudocode and directly comparing mapping choices in Table 9. The corrected main manifold definition, concrete code address and stated limitations also help. These gains are limited by omitted training details and unreconciled EEG reporting between Tables 2 and 8, including the changed reference underlying the ERN percentage. The additional clarity and targeted validation provide a modest net improvement.
